L1-penalized estimation of the precision graph

Source: R/selection.R
mc_graph_penalized.Rd

Fits the GGM layer with an L1 penalty on the edge parameters, $$\hat{\boldsymbol\eta}^{(\lambda)} = \arg\min_{\boldsymbol\eta} \Bigl\{-\ell^p_e(\boldsymbol\eta) + \lambda\sum_{e}|\eta_e|\Bigr\},$$ where \(\ell^p_e\) is the Gaussian working log-criterion of the residual layer (see mc_graph_ploglik), \(K_b=\sum_d\eta_d Z_d\) is the linearly parametrized precision matrix, and the sum runs over the edge parameters only: the diagonal parameters, which set the scale of each response, are not penalized. The penalty is on the accumulated scale of the criterion, so the smallest value that zeroes every edge is \(\lambda_{\max}=n\max_{i<j}|\hat S_{e,ij}|\), with \(\hat S_e\) the sample covariance of the Pearson residuals: for \(\lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}\) the solution is the empty graph. The problem is solved by the proximal gradient method (iterative shrinkage-thresholding): a gradient step \(\boldsymbol\eta+s\boldsymbol\psi_{\boldsymbol\eta}\), with \(\boldsymbol\psi_{\boldsymbol\eta}=\partial\ell^p_e/\partial\boldsymbol\eta\) the Pearson estimating function, followed by soft-thresholding of the edge coordinates at \(s\lambda\). Backtracking halves the step until the precision is positive definite and the sufficient-decrease condition of Beck and Teboulle (2009) holds, under which the penalized objective does not increase, so an admissible matrix alone is not sufficient for accepting an iteration.

Usage

mc_graph_penalized(
  fit,
  lambda,
  max_iter = 300L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  precondition = FALSE,
  kkt_tol = 1e-04,
  start = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph" (GGM layer).

lambda

one finite non-negative penalty parameter, on the accumulated scale of the criterion (see the objective above); lambda = 0 gives the unpenalized fit of the complete graph.

max_iter

maximum number of proximal iterations (default 300).

tol

tolerance on the relative change of the parameter vector, \(\max_d|\eta_d^{+}-\eta_d|/(1+|\eta_d|)\) (default \(10^{-6}\)).

precondition

logical; must be FALSE. TRUE is refused with an error, since the preconditioned step is not a valid proximal step. See the section "Preconditioned step".

kkt_tol

tolerance for the per-unit KKT residual required to certify convergence, in addition to tol on the relative parameter change (default \(10^{-4}\)).

start

optional starting value of the parameter vector, diagonal parameters first and then one per edge of the complete graph, as returned in eta; it must give a positive definite precision. The path of mc_select_lambda uses it for warm starts.

Value

A list with eta (parameter vector, diagonal parameters first and then one per edge of the complete graph), edges (two-column matrix of the pairs whose coefficient is not exactly zero), n_selected (their number), Sigma_b and K_b (fitted covariance and precision), iterations, converged (logical), status ("converged", "kkt_not_certified", "maximum_iterations" or "objective_line_search_failed"), objective (final value of the penalized objective), objective_path (its value along the iterations), kkt (KKT residual, accumulated scale), kkt_unit (per unit, that is, divided by \(n\)) and kkt_tol (the tolerance used).

Convergence certificate

A small relative change of the parameter vector does not by itself certify a stationary point of a non-smooth objective. Convergence is therefore declared only when the relative change is below tol and the per-unit KKT residual is below kkt_tol: when the first holds and the second does not, the iteration goes on. The optimality conditions are \(\hat\Sigma_{b,kk}=\hat S_{e,kk}\) (diagonal), \(n(\hat S_{e,ij}-\hat\Sigma_{b,ij})+\lambda\,\mathrm{sgn}(\hat K_{b,ij})=0\) for a nonzero edge and \(|n(\hat S_{e,ij}-\hat\Sigma_{b,ij})|\le\lambda\) for a zero edge. The KKT residual \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}\) is their largest violation over the coordinates: \(\tfrac{n}{2}|\hat S_{e,kk}-\hat\Sigma_{b,kk}|\) on the diagonal, \(|n(\hat S_{e,ij}-\hat\Sigma_{b,ij})+\lambda\,\mathrm{sgn}(\hat K_{b,ij})|\) on a nonzero edge and \(\max\{|n(\hat S_{e,ij}-\hat\Sigma_{b,ij})|-\lambda,\,0\}\) on a zero edge. The certificate is \(r_{\mathrm{KKT}}/n\le\) kkt_tol. If max_iter is reached in that state the status is "kkt_not_certified", otherwise "maximum_iterations", and in both cases converged is FALSE.

Step size

With \(f=-\ell^p_e\) the smooth part of the objective, whose gradient is \(-\boldsymbol\psi_{\boldsymbol\eta}\), every iteration starts from the step \(s=\{\max_d J_{n,dd}+10^{-8}\}^{-1}\) and halves it until the proximal point \(\boldsymbol\eta^{+}\) gives a positive definite precision and $$f(\boldsymbol\eta^{+})\le f(\boldsymbol\eta)- \boldsymbol\psi_{\boldsymbol\eta}^\top(\boldsymbol\eta^{+}-\boldsymbol\eta) +\frac{1}{2s}\|\boldsymbol\eta^{+}-\boldsymbol\eta\|^2 .$$ The starting step is a scale and not the inverse of a Lipschitz constant; the condition is what guarantees the decrease.

Starting value

The iteration starts from the diagonal fit that is compatible with the empty graph, \(\eta_{kk}=1/\widehat S_{e,kk}\) and every edge at zero, which is also the fit from which the largest penalty of the path is computed. Both need \(\widehat S_{e,kk}>0\) for every response; a response whose Pearson residuals have no variance is refused with an error. The problem has a unique solution, so the start changes the number of iterations and not the target; certified solutions from different starts agree up to the tolerance.

Candidate set

The path is always built over the complete graph on the \(R\) responses, whatever support the supplied fit carries: the penalty, not the input support, decides which edges survive. Passing a fit that was restricted to a sparse support therefore does not restrict the candidates, and the returned edges may include pairs absent from that fit. To keep a support fixed, set it through the edges argument of mc_between_graph and refit, rather than penalizing.

Preconditioned step

A preconditioned step, which multiplies the estimating function by \(J^{-1}\) and then applies coordinatewise soft-thresholding, is not the proximal operator of the L1 penalty in the non-diagonal metric induced by \(J\): it can stop at a point that satisfies the parameter-change test while grossly violating the KKT conditions. precondition = TRUE therefore raises an error, and the fit always uses iterative shrinkage-thresholding, whose certificate is the KKT residual above.

References

Beck, A. and Teboulle, M. (2009). A fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm for linear inverse problems. SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences 2(1), 183–202. doi:10.1137/080716542

Friedman, J., Hastie, T. and Tibshirani, R. (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics 9(3), 432–441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

Yuan, M. and Lin, Y. (2007). Model selection and estimation in the Gaussian graphical model. Biometrika 94(1), 19–35. doi:10.1093/biomet/asm018

See also

mc_select_lambda to choose lambda by an information criterion.

Other structure selection: mc_edge_scores(), mc_graph_stability(), mc_graph_stepwise(), mc_select_lambda()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 300; x <- rnorm(n)
y1 <- rnorm(n); y2 <- 0.6 * y1 + rnorm(n); y3 <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = y1, y2 = y2, y3 = y3, x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
pen <- mc_graph_penalized(f, lambda = 20)
pen$edges
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
pen$status
#> [1] "converged"
# }
